subject.title: contextPruning (mode: cache-ttl) never fires on OpenAI models: isCacheTtlEligibleProvider excludes OpenAI, so the idle-gap tool-result firebreak is dead for the highest-volume provider

question: Should OpenAI use the existing cache-TTL pruning semantics, a retention-aware variant, or a provider-agnostic pruning mode before this issue is fixed?
rationale: Source proves the current gate excludes OpenAI, but enabling pruning for existing OpenAI configs changes retained model context after idle gaps, so the durable policy choice should be explicit before merge.

options.title: Approve retention-aware OpenAI pruning
options.body: Require the candidate fix to align pruning timing with OpenAI cache-retention behavior and include native idle-gap proof before merge.

options.title: Accept generic TTL behavior
options.body: Treat existing `contextPruning.mode: "cache-ttl"` semantics as intentionally applying to OpenAI once eligible, with upgrade impact documented and tested.

options.title: Pursue provider-agnostic pruning
options.body: Reject a provider-eligibility expansion for now and implement a separate pruning mode that does not depend on prompt-cache eligibility.

recommendation.title: Approve retention-aware OpenAI pruning
recommendation.body: Require the candidate fix to align pruning timing with OpenAI cache-retention behavior and include native idle-gap proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current helper, gates, and settings blame to recent work by this login, making them the strongest code-history routing candidate for the policy decision.
